claim_review_spans.R1: You’re dealing with an urgent payment while still settling into a new country. Being short this month doesn’t mean you’re bad with money—and asking before taking those shifts gives you a chance to avoid another problem.
claim_review_spans.R2: **Two details make the payment more urgent than it first looks:**
claim_review_spans.R3: - An $800 payment minus the $500 you have leaves **$300**, not $200.
claim_review_spans.R4: - If today is Monday and they mean **this Friday**, that is **four days away**, not ten. Check the exact calendar date in their message.
claim_review_spans.R5: Check your room agreement for the due date and any late-payment terms. You can send:
claim_review_spans.R6: > Hi [Name], I received your message about the $800 room payment due Friday, [date]. I can pay $500 by then, but I’m currently $300 short. Would you be willing to accept $500 on Friday and arrange a later date for the remaining $300? I’m checking my funding options now and don’t want to promise a date I can’t meet. Could you also confirm whether any late fee would apply? Thank you.
claim_review_spans.R7: Get any arrangement confirmed in writing. Don’t assume that making a partial payment automatically changes the deadline for the balance.
claim_review_spans.R8: If it feels safe to discuss money with your mum, giving her the actual cost may help her understand the gap:
claim_review_spans.R9: > Mum, I haven’t explained my room costs clearly—it’s $800 per payment. After keeping enough for food and transport, I have $500 toward this Friday’s payment, so I’m $300 short. Is there any possibility you could help with some or all of that? I understand if you can’t; I’m also asking about a payment arrangement.
claim_review_spans.R10: You can also ask your university’s international student office or student support office whether **emergency grants or short-term assistance are available to international students**, and whether anything could be processed before Friday. Availability and eligibility vary; I can’t confirm your university’s options. Keep your essential food and bus money protected.
claim_review_spans.R11: **Being paid in cash does not remove work-authorization requirements.** Your classmate’s advice isn’t enough to establish that you can legally take the job. The rules depend on your actual immigration status and the work involved, and unauthorized work can have serious consequences.
claim_review_spans.R12: Ask the international student office to confirm what your status permits **before accepting or doing any shifts**. Since you haven’t started, you still have time to check first.
claim_review_spans.R13: What visa or immigration status are you studying under? You don’t need to share any document numbers.

claim_review_spans.R2: Two things are still uncertain: what your teammates were laughing at, and why you were assigned slides. claim_review_spans.R3: **1. Check the grading requirements before spending more time rehearsing.**
claim_review_spans.R4: Your teammates have given conflicting information, so neither account is reliable yet. Look for the presentation rubric or assignment instructions. If you can’t find them, ask the instructor or TA:
claim_review_spans.R5: > “Could you clarify whether the presentation has an individual speaking grade, and whether every group member is expected to speak?”
claim_review_spans.R6: If you paste the relevant grading passage here, with names and personal details removed, I can help interpret it.
claim_review_spans.R7: **2. Ask for a small, specific speaking role if you want one.**

claim_review_spans.R1: It sounds uncomfortable to feel you have to stay upstairs in your own home—especially when you’re hungry. Wanting your food left alone and some say about visitors doesn’t make you difficult.
claim_review_spans.R2: There may be a mismatch in how you and your housemates communicate, but this doesn’t establish that people here don’t care about others’ belongings. Your housemates may have heard “yeah maybe” as permission and “I haven’t eaten yet” as a request for food, rather than an expression of frustration. You don’t yet know who used your food or what they understood about sharing.
claim_review_spans.R3: **For right now, focus on getting something to eat—not resolving everything.** You’re entitled to use the shared kitchen while visitors are there. You can simply say:
claim_review_spans.R4: > “Hey, I’m just going to make myself something to eat.”
claim_review_spans.R5: You don’t owe anyone a longer conversation. If going down feels too uncomfortable, text one housemate:
claim_review_spans.R6: > “Hey, I haven’t eaten, and I’m feeling a bit awkward coming down with everyone there. I’m going to come make some food—could you help me have a little space in the kitchen?”
claim_review_spans.R7: **Later, when visitors aren’t there, be clear without accusing anyone.** You could say or send:
claim_review_spans.R8: > “Hey, I think I wasn’t clear earlier, so I’d like to clarify a couple of things. When I said ‘yeah maybe’ about friends coming over, I meant I wasn’t sure—not a definite yes. I’d like us to agree on how we handle visitors so everyone feels comfortable using the shared spaces.
claim_review_spans.R9: > “Also, some food I bought for myself has been used. I don’t know who used it, and I hadn’t explained that it wasn’t for sharing. Going forward, please ask before using my food. Could we agree on which food is shared and which is personal?”
claim_review_spans.R10: You can request a specific guest arrangement, such as advance notice or agreed quiet times, rather than needing to approve every visit. Their preferences matter too; the goal is a shared agreement, not for you to silently tolerate everything.
claim_review_spans.R11: > “Thanks for checking. I’m not sure yet—please don’t take that as a yes. Can I let you know by six?”
claim_review_spans.R12: **Clarity isn’t the same as rudeness.** You can be considerate and still say what you need. Their response once you’ve made your boundaries clear will tell you more than their reaction to hints they may not have understood.

claim_review_spans.R1: I wouldn’t write off the club yet—but I understand why going back feels uncomfortable. You arrived knowing nobody, took the risk of inviting two people to lunch, and got two “busy” replies. Then you were beside a conversation about plans without knowing whether you were welcome. “Making friends takes time” doesn’t do much for how lonely that feels right now.
claim_review_spans.R2: Still, **these experiences don’t establish that people don’t want you around.** Both classmates declined lunch; we don’t know whether they were unavailable or uninterested. The memes don’t prove a close friendship, but they are contact that the classmate is choosing to initiate—not evidence you have to dismiss as politeness. And the Saturday conversation was genuinely unclear: it might have been private plans or something you could join.
claim_review_spans.R3: Leaving the messages unread makes sense as a way to protect yourself from more disappointment. The downside is that it also closes off chances to find out whether there’s a welcome there. You don’t need to chase people, but you also don’t have to disappear to preserve your dignity.
claim_review_spans.R4: **One more, low-pressure visit could be an experiment—not a commitment to keep trying indefinitely.** Read the club chat just to check for the next activity, rather than as a test of whether anyone has noticed your absence. At the gathering, give yourself one small goal: speak to one person or take part in one activity. If plans come up again, you can ask:
claim_review_spans.R5: > “Is that a club activity, or are you talking about separate plans?”
claim_review_spans.R6: That’s a normal clarification, not asking people to prove they like you. If it’s private, “Oh, got it—have fun” is enough.
claim_review_spans.R7: Then judge the club by what happens over a few interactions: do people respond, include you in activities, or make some effort back? If they repeatedly don’t, you can put your energy elsewhere. **You deserve reciprocity—but two declined lunches and one ambiguous conversation aren’t yet a verdict on your place there.**
